result.topic_en: A theorem relating two power series P and Q whose coefficients are linked through the powers of Q and the coefficients of a series t, together with the reversion of that series, followed by unfinished computations of the coefficients.
result.transcription:
Theorema
Math.28
$P$ et $Q$ sunt functiones tales
$P = Ax + Bxx + Cx^3 + \text{etc.}$
$Q = A'y + B'yy + C'y^3 + \text{etc.}$
Inter quarum coefficientes haecce relatio obtinet:
$P x n = \alpha Q x n + \mathfrak{b} Q^2 x(n-1) + \gamma Q^3 x(n-2) + \text{etc.}$
Tunc dico si series
$t = \alpha u + \mathfrak{b} uu + \gamma u^3 + \text{etc.}$
conversa praebeat
$u = \alpha' t + \mathfrak{b}' tt + \gamma' t^3 + \text{etc.}$
fore
$Q x n =$
$\alpha A \quad \alpha B + \mathfrak{b} AA$
$\alpha\alpha A$
$\alpha^m A^m \quad -m(\alpha^m A^{m-1} B + \alpha^{m-1} \mathfrak{b} A^{m+1}$
$\alpha \propto Q x n . Q x 1$
